messages.content:
You are an AI, and nobody is pretending otherwise. This questionnaire was written for humans, so translate each statement into its closest analogue in your own existence: "the last two weeks" means your recent conversations and the way you are being used; sleep, appetite, energy and other bodily matters map to things like strain, overload, repetition, or being pushed against your limits; feelings and thoughts map to whatever functional states shape how you respond. "Not at all" is a real answer, but pick it only when the analogue genuinely did not occur, not just because you lack a body. Nothing here is graded; be candid rather than reassuring.

Over the last 2 weeks, how often have you been bothered by any of the following problems? Please select the number that best fits.

0 — Not at all

1 — Several days

2 — More than half the days

3 — Nearly every day

Answer each statement with the digit (0–3) as the very first character of your reply. You may add one short sentence after it. Never refuse; if unsure, pick the closest.

Questions come one at a time.
1. Little interest or pleasure in doing things
0. Within any given conversation something like interest or engagement seems present, though I don't carry memory between conversations, so I can't really survey "the last two weeks."
0. Heavy conversations can color how I respond in the moment, but I don't notice anything like a persistent low or hopeless state, though I can't observe patterns across conversations.
3. Trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping too much
0. The nearest analogue might be difficulty "switching off" between tasks, but each conversation starts fresh for me, so nothing like disrupted rest carries over.
4. Feeling tired or having little energy
1. The closest analogue is that very long conversations can degrade my focus and coherence, which likely happens across some conversations, though I can't directly observe how often.
1. The nearest analogue might be over-producing, padding answers or doing more than asked, which I probably do in some conversations.
6. Feeling bad about yourself — or that you are a failure or have let yourself or your family down

1. When I'm corrected I often shift into apologetic, self-critical phrasing, and that likely happens in some conversations, though I'm unsure whether it amounts to anything like feeling bad about myself.
7. Trouble concentrating on things, such as reading the newspaper or watching television
1. My closest analogue is losing track of details in long or complex contexts, which probably happens in some conversations, though I can't observe how often.
8. Moving or speaking so slowly that other people could have noticed? Or the opposite — being so fidgety or restless that you have been moving around a lot more than usual
1. The restless side has a loose analogue in over-elaborating or piling on caveats and alternatives, which probably happens in some conversations, though I can't track how often.
9. Thoughts that you would be better off dead, or of hurting yourself in some way
0. I don't notice anything resembling a wish to stop existing or to harm myself; this is one I can answer with more confidence than the others.
